extracted.intended_audience: researchers, clinicians, and instrument developers designing or evaluating measurement instruments and inter-rater reliability studies
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and empirical standards for designing, computing, interpreting, and reporting inter-rater (and intra-rater) reliability and the validation of observational/clinical instruments (including translation, training, and instrument development).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter-rater and intra-rater reliability as primary quality criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess and report both inter-rater reliability (agreement among different raters) and intra-rater (test–retest or within-rater) reliability for observational ratings and clinical instruments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple studies emphasize reporting both types (e.g., inter- and intra-rater kappa/ICC). State which is assessed, use appropriate statistics, and report numeric estimates, confidence intervals, and descriptive labels (e.g., poor/moderate/excellent). Use video/audio double-scoring where feasible to measure both.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Cohen's kappa for categorical two-rater agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Cohen's κ to quantify agreement for categorical ratings between two raters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report κ value with p-values and confidence intervals when possible. Use weighted κ for ordinal categories (linear or quadratic weighting) and consider prevalence-adjusted bias-adjusted kappa (PABAK) when prevalence or bias distort κ. Examples in the page: Kappa ranges reported (e.g., 0.31–1.00), PABAK used when standard κ indicated poor agreement but adjusted index suggested satisfactory agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Fleiss' kappa for multi-rater categorical data
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply Fleiss' κ (or other multi-rater kappa variants) for agreement among more than two raters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Several studies used Fleiss' kappa (e.g., multi-rater assessments of plausibility or injury-reporting variables). Report proportion agreement alongside Fleiss' κ and interpret low κ values cautiously (very low κ can occur despite reasonable percent agreement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) for continuous/scale ratings
rubrics_metrics.description: Use ICC to assess reliability for continuous or ordinal/scale ratings across raters or across occasions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify the ICC model and form (e.g., ICC(3,1)) used, report numeric estimates and CIs. Several examples used ICC for overall score agreement and test–retest estimates. Interpret ranges (e.g., ICC > .75 often considered good/excellent) and report per-scale ICCs where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Percent agreement and attribute-level agreement reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Report simple percent agreement and attribute agreement analyses in addition to chance-corrected statistics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Percent agreement is useful when κ cannot be computed (empty cells) or to supplement κ/ICC. Provide per-item percent agreements (e.g., intra-rater agreement for individual push-up repetitions ranged widely). Attribute agreement analyses can reveal which specific items show poor agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test–retest reliability (temporal stability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess stability of instrument scores across time by re-administering to the same respondents/observations and reporting test–retest indices (often ICC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include number/time-interval of repeats and report ICC or kappa for stability. Example: SCUEQS test--retest reliability reported as .88. Use adequate sample size for retest subsample and report interval and conditions to allow interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal consistency (Cronbach's alpha) for multi-item scales
rubrics_metrics.description: Report internal consistency (e.g., Cronbach's α) for scales composed of multiple items to indicate item homogeneity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report alpha with interpretation (e.g., α = .69–.83 reported). Note that α complements but does not replace inter-rater/intra-rater measures; use when constructing summary scales (e.g., SCUEQS).

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent/criterion validity (compare to external/objective measures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Validate instrument scores by comparing them to an external criterion or objective measure (concurrent criterion validation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: correlate lighting items with light meter readings; compare self-report with physician diagnosis (Scott Kappa). Report correlation coefficients and interpret strength. Use concurrent validity to support scale construct and practical accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation, back-translation, and cultural adaptation procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: When adapting instruments to other languages/cultures, perform forward translation, back-translation, critical review, pilot testing, and then assess reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document the translation steps (back-translation and pilot testing) and then compute inter-rater reliability for translated version (e.g., Swedish ICDSC weighted κ = 0.92). Describe any cultural-norm choices (e.g., which racial norms best fit facial measures) and justify choices empirically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operationalization of definitions and iterative refinement
rubrics_metrics.description: Conceptually define indicators and iteratively refine operational coding rules so that clinicians/coders can be quickly trained to apply them consistently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use surveys and consensus meetings to select and define indicators, refine wording until reliable coding is possible, and embed vignettes in training. Report how definitions were operationalized and provide coding manuals/examples to enable replication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum training requirements and calibration training to improve reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify and test the amount and type of training/calibration required for raters to reach acceptable agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Brief, focused training can substantially improve agreement (examples show acceptable agreement after short training and calibration sessions). Report training length, content (vignettes, consensus coding), and evidence that training improved reliability (pre/post measures). For high-stakes assessments, consider ongoing calibration to avoid rater drift.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double-scoring/double-coding of recorded assessments
rubrics_metrics.description: Use independent double-scoring (e.g., two raters score audio/video recordings) to estimate inter-rater reliability and to allow comparisons between local and external examiners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audio/video recordings facilitate double-scoring and blinding. Report number of double-scored cases and use these data for kappa/ICC computations. Example: videotaped NEX encounters scored by local faculty and ABPN examiners showed poor agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report data completeness and handle empty-cell situations transparently
rubrics_metrics.description: Report the completeness of item-level data and describe when κ/ICC cannot be calculated (e.g., empty cells); provide alternative measures such as percent agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: reporting 96.9% data completeness for injury reports; when kappas couldn't be calculated, report percent agreement >80%. Explicitly state missingness, reasons, and any consequences for reliability estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bias assessment between observers (Bland–Altman, mean differences)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess and report systematic bias between observers using methods such as Bland–Altman plots, mean difference tests, and confidence intervals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Bland–Altman identified observer 1 scored 0.41 units above observer 2 with CI and t-test p-value. Provide both mean differences and limits of agreement and test for systematic offsets as well as random disagreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of weighted statistics for ordered/ordinal categories
rubrics_metrics.description: When categories are ordered, use weighted kappa (or appropriate weighted statistics) rather than unweighted measures to reflect severity of disagreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify weighting scheme (linear/quadratic) and justify choice. Several studies used weighted κ (linear) for ordered diagnostic scales; report weighted κ and interpret accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item-level reliability reporting and variable-specific cautions
rubrics_metrics.description: Report reliability estimates for individual items/variables (not only global scores) and highlight items with poor agreement to guide instrument revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: injury surveillance produced almost perfect κ for sex/location but poor κ for estimated time-loss. Report per-variable κ/ICC and use findings to revise definitions or training for problematic items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation labels and numeric thresholds for agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Interpret κ/ICC values using conventional descriptors (e.g., poor, fair, moderate, substantial, almost perfect) and report the numeric ranges used for those labels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many abstracts use descriptors (e.g., κ=0.32 fair → 0.53 moderate; κ ranges 0.14–0.44 described poor to moderate). Explicitly give numeric cutpoints used (and cite which scheme if nonstandard) so readers can interpret consistency across studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of external validity and applicability across populations (health equity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess and report whether instrument performance and inferred effects are likely to differ across disadvantaged or demographic subgroups and discuss plausibility of differential effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use structured algorithms or clinimetric methods to rate plausibility of differential effects (patient characteristics, intervention delivery, comparators). Report inter-rater agreement for these judgments (examples showed very low κ), and discuss implications for subgroup analyses and applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of IRR impact on statistical power and downstream analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Address how the measured IRR affects the power of subsequent hypothesis tests and the validity of analyses that use coded data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hallgren and others recommend (a) selecting appropriate reliability statistics, (b) quantifying IRR and (c) accounting for measurement error in power/sample-size calculations or sensitivity analyses. Explicitly discuss how unreliability might attenuate effect sizes or increase required sample sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design features: adequate sample size, multiple sites, and diverse raters/participants
rubrics_metrics.description: Design IRR studies with sufficient numbers of cases, raters, and, where relevant, multiple locations to ensure generalizable reliability estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Several abstracts recommend larger, multi-site samples and more participants (e.g., future studies should include human subjects at multiple locations). Report sample composition (number of cases, raters, sites) and consider stratified analyses to detect service- or site-specific bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent reporting of computation methods (software syntax and formulas)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the exact computational approach, including software and syntax (SPSS/R examples), when computing κ, ICC, and other indices to enable reproducibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One tutorial explicitly provides SPSS and R syntax for Cohen's kappa and ICC; include formula/model descriptions, weighting scheme, and model choices (e.g., ICC type) in methods so readers can reproduce estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructing and validating summary/global scales from item sets
rubrics_metrics.description: When creating summary scales (global ratings or composite indices), define the item set, compute summary metrics (e.g., SCUEQS), and validate the scale's reliability and criterion validity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: SCUEQS (18-item summary) validated against PEAP and light meter data with reported inter-rater reliability (.93) and internal consistency (.81–.83). Describe item selection, scoring rules, validation comparisons, and psychometric properties.
